Nov 20, 2026

Agents SDK now supports Pi 1.6 with tools that wait without keeping your agent awake

Agents

Agents SDK v0.34.0 upgrades PiHarness to Pi 1.6 ↗︎. A Pi tool can now wait for a person, a deadline, or another session without keeping the Durable Object awake, and a session can start from a history that your application already has.

Tools that wait

  • Park until a signal or a deadline. A tool can return a park instead of a result, and Pi runs it again when a signal arrives or the deadline passes. While it waits, the call holds no invocation, so the Durable Object can hibernate. Deliver signals with the new harness.signal(). Refer to Tools that wait.
  • Wait for a subagent. submit() and continue() take notify, so a parked tool wakes when another session's input settles. Refer to Wait for a subagent.
  • Approval gates. A beforeTool hook can park a tool call before it runs, for example until a person approves it.

Session updates

  • Start a session from an existing history. harness.root(), sessions.create(), and sessions.fork() take Pi's init, which writes messages into the transcript in the commit that creates the session. The root session is now created on its first use, so harness.root() can seed it. Refer to Seed a session with an existing history.
  • Keep queued input across an abort. With submit(input, { onAbort: "keep" }), stopping an answer does not drop the message that the user or another agent sent next.
  • Steadier runs. Pi retries more dropped provider connections. When Anthropic can no longer continue a message thread, agents/models/pi-ai sends the whole conversation again instead of failing the turn. PiHarness.dispose() frees Pi AI's per-session state.

Wait for a person's answer

This tool asks the user a question, then parks until your agent delivers the answer:

While the question is open, the session's run is still going, and the object can hibernate or be evicted. harness.signal() wakes the object, and Pi runs the tool again with the answer.

Other changes

  • MCP re-authorization. A request that needs the user to sign in again throws MCPAuthorizationRequiredError with a link. A failed server stays failed until you call the new reconnectMcpServer(id). Refer to Failures and reconnecting.
  • Failed requests no longer send error details. A failed request gets a generic 500 response, and a failed WebSocket upgrade closes with code 1011. Use onFetchError() to choose the response. Refer to Failed requests.
  • Chat fixes. Stop, clear, regenerate, and resume now work across tabs and during recovery.
  • Scheduling fixes. A schedule, queue item, or Task run that is cancelled or replaced no longer runs again.
  • Models. ai.image() and Pi AI's ai.images() run the FLUX.2 image models. claudeCode() defaults to claude-sonnet-5-5. Examples move off the Workers AI models retired on November 20, 2026.

Upgrade

Once a conversation runs on Pi 1.6, Pi 1.5 cannot run its tool calls or model requests. After upgrading, roll forward to fix deployment issues rather than rolling back to Pi 1.5.

Deliver signals with harness.signal() instead of (await harness.pi()).signal(), and call harness.root() before you reach the root session through harness.pi(). If you use Pi Durable directly, RunEndTask is now HookTask, and code mode namespaces come from Extension.namespace. Refer to the Pi Durable 1.6.0 changelog ↗︎ for the full list of breaking changes.

If you use the MCP client, catch MCPAuthorizationRequiredError and send the user to error.authUrl, and give users a way to call reconnectMcpServer(id) for a failed server. If you relied on error details in failed responses, implement onFetchError().

The Agents SDK v0.34.0 changelog ↗︎ has step-by-step upgrade instructions. Point your coding agent at them and upgrade today:

Nov 20, 2026

Run custom scripts in Browser Run with /script

Browser Run

Browser Run now runs custom browser automation written with Playwright, Puppeteer, or the raw Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) in a single API request, with the new /script endpoints. Submit a JavaScript function, and Browser Run executes it in an isolated Worker connected to a browser session, so you do not need to deploy a Worker.

  • POST /script acquires a browser, runs your function, and returns its result as { "success": true, "result": ... }. The session and page are returned in the cf-browser-session-id and cf-browser-target-id response headers (except Kitesurf runs).
  • POST /script/<sessionId> runs follow-up scripts in a session you already hold, from /script or from POST /devtools/browser. Pass targetId to attach to a specific page, or create extra pages to run scripts concurrently in one session.
  • Session launch options (keep_alive, recording, lab) go in the /script query string. Use browser=kitesurf to run a CDP script on Kitesurf.
  • From a Worker, call the same endpoints through the browser binding with env.BROWSER.script(), without an API token.
  • From the Cloudflare dashboard, write and run scripts against a live browser in Script Studio, without an API token.
  • Neither endpoint closes the session after your script runs. Close it with DELETE /devtools/browser/<sessionId> or browser.close(). Otherwise, it ends at its idle timeout.

For more information, refer to Custom scripts.

Nov 19, 2026

Capture PDFs, links, scraped elements, and extracted JSON with /snapshot

Browser Run

Browser Run's /snapshot endpoint can now return four more formats from a single page load: pdf, links, scrape, and json. Before, /snapshot returned HTML, screenshots, Markdown, and the accessibility tree, so a workflow that also needed a PDF or structured data had to prepare the same page again in a second request.

Use the new formats when you need to:

  • PDF: print the page, with the same pdfOptions as the /pdf endpoint.
  • Links: collect the links on the page, with the same visibleLinksOnly and excludeExternalLinks options as /links.
  • Scraped elements: return the elements matched by elements, the same payload as /scrape. elements is required when you request it.
  • Extracted JSON: extract structured data from the page HTML with Workers AI, with the same prompt, response_format, and custom_ai fields as /json. prompt or response_format is required, and the request incurs Workers AI usage.

Request them through formats, the same way as the existing formats. This example returns a PDF, the page links, and the text of each paragraph:

Formats are captured in a fixed order rather than the order of the formats array, and the PDF is printed last because print handlers can change the page. A live page can change between captures, and any format that fails fails the whole request. For JSON snapshots, one actionTimeout budget (default 60 seconds, maximum 120 seconds) covers navigation, captures, retries, and the AI request.

You still need to request at least two distinct formats. If you only need one, use the corresponding single-format endpoint.

Refer to the /snapshot documentation for the full list of accepted values and options.

Nov 18, 2026

Attach images, PDFs, and text files to Agent Lee

Agent Lee

You can now attach files to a message in Agent Lee. Share a screenshot of an error, a PDF, or a log, HAR, or configuration file, and Agent Lee reads it as part of your question.

Previously, you had to describe what you were seeing or paste file contents into the chat by hand. A screenshot of a dashboard error or a long log was hard to get across that way.

How it works

  • Select the paperclip next to the message box, paste an image, or drag files onto the chat panel.
  • Each file appears as a chip above the message box. Remove any you did not mean to add, then send your message.
  • Agent Lee reads images directly, converts PDFs to text and reads them from the start, and reads text files in full or, for long files, from the start and the end.

Example requests:

  • "Here is a screenshot of the error I get when I open my site. What is wrong?"
  • "This HAR file is from a slow page load. Which requests are taking the longest?"
  • "Here is the error log from my Worker. What is causing these failures?"

Good to know

  • Supported files. PNG, JPEG, and WebP images up to 3.5 MiB, PDFs up to 5 MiB, and text files (.txt, .log, .json, .har, .csv, .yaml, .yml, .toml, .md, .xml) up to 100 MiB. You can attach up to four files per message, up to 14 MiB in total after trimming.
  • Text files are trimmed in your browser. A text file over 1 MiB (2 MiB for JSON, HAR, YAML, TOML, and XML) keeps its first and last lines. HAR files are always compacted before sending: request and response bodies and cookies are removed, and credential headers such as Authorization and Cookie are replaced with [redacted].
  • Scanned PDFs are not read. Agent Lee reads the text in a PDF. A PDF that is only scanned images, with no text layer, cannot be read.
  • Older attachments age out. Agent Lee keeps attachments from your most recent messages in view. Attach a file again to bring an older one back into the conversation.
  • Attachments are stored with the conversation. When an attachment ages out, it is removed from the stored conversation. Do not attach files that contain passwords, API tokens, or other secrets. For how Agent Lee uses your data, refer to Data usage.

Agent Lee remains in beta. Features and behaviors may change as the product evolves.

For details, refer to Agent Lee.

Nov 17, 2026

AI Search can generate file summaries during indexing

AI Search

AI Search can now summarize your files while it indexes them. For each text document that produces at least three chunks, AI Search uses a large language model (LLM) to generate a summary, topics, and keywords:

  • The summary and keywords are stored in the item's context metadata. A context value you already set is kept.
  • The topics are added to the context header of the file's chunks to help retrieval.

Turn on file summaries in the dashboard, or set indexing_options.file_summary to true when you create or update an instance. File summaries are off by default, and changing the setting triggers a full reindex.

indexing_options is replaced as a whole on every update. Include the current value of every option, or the options you leave out return to their defaults.

The LLM costs are billed to your account. File summaries are not part of the AI Search ingestion allotment. AI Search uses a Workers AI model suited to summarization and calls it through your instance's AI Gateway, or the default gateway if none is set, and the calls are billed as Workers AI usage. Each new or modified file is summarized once, so costs grow with the amount of content you index.

For more information, refer to File summaries.

Browser Run Quick Actions now work in local development

Browser Run

You can now test Browser Run Quick Actions locally. Under npx wrangler dev, the browser binding's .quickAction() method runs against a Chrome instance on your machine. Before, .quickAction() worked only in remote mode, and local calls failed with The RPC receiver does not implement the method "quickAction".

Note

There are currently two limitations in the local simulation:

For details, refer to Test Quick Actions locally.

Nov 12, 2026

Kitesurf is now open source

Browser Run

Kitesurf ↗︎, Cloudflare's browser engine for AI agents, is now open source on GitHub ↗︎ under the Apache 2.0 license. You can inspect the source, run it locally, and deploy your own instance to your Cloudflare account.

Kitesurf runs entirely on Cloudflare Workers. It parses HTML, applies CSS, executes page JavaScript, and renders screenshots without a browser container. It supports the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), so you can connect clients such as Puppeteer.

Kitesurf is still experimental and under heavy development. The team continues to improve web standards support, rendering fidelity, and performance.

Run locally or deploy to your account

Developers can run Kitesurf locally with Wrangler. After following the build requirements and setup instructions ↗︎, run pnpm run dev. This builds the engine and starts wrangler dev.

To run your own instance on Cloudflare, follow the deployment instructions ↗︎. Protect your deployment with Cloudflare Access or another authentication layer. Kitesurf does not provide built-in authentication.

Important

Kitesurf requires Cloudflare Dynamic Workers to create isolated Workers for pages. Dynamic Workers are part of the Workers Paid plan. A Workers Paid plan is required to run Kitesurf on Cloudflare. Local development uses wrangler dev.

Contribute and follow progress

Contributions and pull requests are welcome. The team remains focused on compatibility, reliability, and performance, with limited review capacity. Keep changes focused and follow the contribution guidelines ↗︎, including opening an issue and getting vouched by a maintainer before submitting a pull request.

Visit kitesurf.dev ↗︎, the main Kitesurf website and playground. Track Web Platform Tests (WPT) progress ↗︎ and performance benchmarks ↗︎ as development continues.

For background and technical details, refer to the introductory blog post ↗︎ and the Kitesurf update ↗︎. To use Kitesurf through Browser Run, refer to the Kitesurf documentation.

Nov 12, 2026

EmbeddingGemma 2 now available on Workers AI

Workers AI

@cf/google/embeddinggemma-2 is now available on Workers AI. EmbeddingGemma 2 is an open multimodal embedding model from Google DeepMind. It maps text (including code), images, video, and audio into a single 768-dimensional vector space, so you can search a mixed collection of products, documents, and media with one text query.

Key capabilities:

  • Multimodal: Embed text, images, video, audio, or any combination of them in one input. Every embedding shares the same vector space.
  • Multilingual and code: Understands more than 100 languages and improves code retrieval over the original EmbeddingGemma.
  • Flexible dimensions: Set dimensions to 128, 256, or 512 to return shorter vectors and reduce storage, with a small cost to quality.
  • Long context: An 8,192 token context window, shared across all content in an input.
  • Task prefixes: Add short instructions such as task: search result | query: ... to tune embeddings for search, classification, clustering, or similarity.

Send text with input. Send images, video, and audio as base64 data URIs in messages:

Pricing is $0.0017 per million input tokens.

For more information, refer to the EmbeddingGemma 2 model page and pricing.

Nov 12, 2026

Inkling 2 Small now available on Workers AI

Workers AI

@cf/thinkingmachines/inkling-2-small is now available on Workers AI. Inkling 2 Small is the second generation of Inkling models from Thinking Machines Lab, and the first frontier open model from a US lab on Workers AI.

Inkling 2 Small is more capable than the previous generation. It is a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 594B total parameters and 18B active parameters. Thinking Machines trained it much faster than previous models because of improvements to their pre-training and infrastructure.

Inkling 2 Small works well for:

  • Agentic coding: Plan, write, and edit code across multi-step tasks.
  • Vision understanding: Interpret images sent alongside text in the same request.
  • General agentic knowledge work: Research, analyze, and act on information with tools.

Key capabilities:

  • Vision: Accepts text and image inputs.
  • Reasoning: Reasoning is on by default at high effort. Set reasoning_effort to max, medium, low, or minimal to change the effort, or to none to turn reasoning off.
  • Function calling: Build agents that invoke tools and APIs across multiple conversation turns.
  • Long context: A full 1,048,576 token context window.

Inkling 2 Small requires the Workers Paid plan or prepaid AI Gateway credits. The default rate limit is 20 requests per minute with standard Workers AI billing and 50 requests per minute with prepaid AI Gateway credits. For details, refer to limits.

Use Inkling 2 Small through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()), the REST API, the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or AI Gateway.

For more information, refer to the Inkling 2 Small model page and pricing.

Nov 3, 2026

Agents SDK now supports Pi 1.5 with fewer storage writes and lower memory use

Agents

Agents SDK v0.33.0 upgrades PiHarness to Pi 1.5 ↗︎. The release reduces storage transactions while streaming, improves throughput across many sessions, and reduces memory use when streaming large tool calls.

Performance improvements

  • Far fewer storage writes while streaming. Pi stores streamed answers and tool output in batches, within a second of each update, instead of on every update. Over SQLite, this cuts storage transactions by about 27x for long answers and 5.7x for turns with parallel tools, and CPU by about a quarter.
  • Higher throughput across many sessions. Pi's scheduler no longer rechecks every conversation on each commit. In a SQLite benchmark with 2,048 sessions, one Pi harness went from 88 to 459 agent runs per second.
  • Less memory on large answers. Streaming a 500 KB tool call used to take about 20 seconds of CPU and a 100 MB heap. Pi now appends new text instead of copying it on every update.

Streaming updates remain visible immediately, but are persisted in batches. With the default settings, a crash can lose up to about one second of streamed progress. Refer to Recovery to configure this interval.

Session and tool updates

  • A view of each session. session.watch() replaces session.events(). It returns the newest transcript entries and the session's live state, such as the answer being streamed, running tools, and why the last run ended without an answer.
  • Continue without adding a message. The new session.continue() API starts a new run using the existing transcript, for example after a model error or when a run reaches its turn limit.
  • Turn limit. defaults.maxTurns caps the tool rounds a run can take in new sessions.
  • Tasks that keep crashing end. Pi now ends a task cut off by its restart limit instead of parking it. retry() and the parked status are removed.
  • Browser in Pi's code mode. Scripts in Pi's code mode can call browserTool and pass its screenshots to image(). browserTool also stops when the harness aborts its call.

Continue an unanswered conversation

For an existing session and submission operationId, check the result before offering a continuation. For example, after resolving a model error:

This starts a new run without appending a user message. The session must be idle. If the transcript already ends in an answer, the operation returns unanswered with reason nothing_to_answer. Refer to Work with sessions.

Upgrade

Once a conversation runs on Pi 1.5, Pi 1.4 cannot read it. After upgrading, roll forward to fix deployment issues rather than rolling back to Pi 1.4.

Update callers of session.events() to use session.watch(), and remove uses of retry() and the parked status. Refer to the Pi Durable 1.5.0 changelog ↗︎ for the full list of breaking changes.

The Agents SDK v0.33.0 changelog ↗︎ has step-by-step upgrade instructions. Point your coding agent at them and upgrade today:

Nov 3, 2026

New AI Gateways require authentication

AI Gateway

New AI Gateways now require authentication to prevent unauthorized requests. Once authentication is on, you cannot turn it off through the dashboard or API.

When you create a new AI Gateway through the API, authentication is on by default. You can leave out the authentication field or set it to true. If you set it to false, the API returns HTTP 400.

When you update an existing gateway, leaving out authentication keeps its current setting. If you try to turn off authentication after it is on, the API returns HTTP 400.

Existing gateways with authentication turned off can continue without it. You can turn it on in your gateway settings or include authentication: true in a gateway update request:

Before turning authentication on, configure HTTP clients to send a valid Cloudflare API token. Requests through Workers bindings remain pre-authenticated.

For setup instructions and supported authorization headers, refer to AI Gateway authentication.

Nov 3, 2026

Crawl results include URL outcomes and robots.txt diagnostics

Browser Run

Browser Run /crawl results now include more detailed diagnostics. Each URL record can include an outcome that identifies the specific processing result, such as success, robots_disallowed, timeout, or page_error.

The job-level robots array reports the robots.txt state for up to 50 origins encountered by the crawl. Each entry includes the origin, whether usable rules were available, and the HTTP status when the crawler received a response.

For field definitions and all possible outcome values, refer to URL outcomes and robots.txt diagnostics.

For rates and included usage, refer to Limits & pricing.

Default sync interval is now 24 hours

The default sync interval for AI Search instances is changing from 6 hours to 24 hours. You can still choose any supported interval, from 15 minutes to 24 hours, with the Sync interval setting in your instance settings or the sync_interval field in the API.

For details, refer to Sync interval.

Oct 30, 2026

Browser Run now runs Chrome 152

Browser Run

Browser Run now runs Chrome 152 by default. Your sessions get current web platform features, rendering fixes, and security patches. You do not need to change your code.

This release also includes the following improvements:

  • Updated default User-Agent. The default User-Agent for Quick Actions now reports Chrome 152 instead of Chrome 119. If you allowlist or match the Browser Run User-Agent, update your rules. You can still set your own value with the userAgent parameter. Refer to Automatic request headers.
  • Better site compatibility. Quick Actions requests now look more like requests from a regular Chrome browser, so fewer sites block them.
  • Large response headers. Pages that return large response headers now load correctly.
  • Updated root certificates. Browser Run removed distrusted root certificates from its trust store.
  • Absolute links. /links now returns absolute URLs, and links-only crawls now follow relative links.
  • Better Markdown output. /markdown and crawl Markdown output now keep code block languages.
  • Clearer errors. Quick Actions that time out now return a consistent error. Outbound Workers that throw an exception now return an HTTP error to the browser.

For more information, refer to the Browser Run documentation.

Oct 29, 2026

Agents SDK: Agent Skills are files in your agent's Workspace

Agents

Agent Skills in the Cloudflare Agents SDK are now files. Write a folder with a SKILL.md into your agent's Computer ↗︎ Workspace, under /workspace/.agents/skills/, and the agent can use it on its next turn. You do not need a build step or a deploy, and the agent can write its own skills.

This release includes:

  • Three sources. Load skills from a Computer Workspace, an R2 bucket, or code. Think lists every source again before each turn.
  • The open format. Every SKILL.md is checked against the Agent Skills specification ↗︎. As the specification's guide for agents recommends, a skill that breaks a rule still loads, with a logged warning. Use parseSkill() to check a skill before you write it.
  • Scripts in the Workspace. Skill scripts are Workspace files, and the model runs them with the Workspace exec tool. Refer to Execution.
  • Skill tools for any harness. Use the same activate_skill and read_skill_resource tools in Think, Pi Durable, or the AI SDK. Refer to Skills tools.
  • Warm prompt caches. When a skill changes mid-conversation, Think sends the new catalog as a reminder instead of rebuilding the cached system prompt. An overridden getSystemPrompt() now stays at the top of the system prompt, above context blocks.

This is a breaking change for code that uses agents/skills directly. The agents:skills Vite import, agents/skills/compile, SkillRegistry, and Think's skillWorkspace are removed, and runner() moved to agents/skills/runner. Install Agents SDK v0.32.0 ↗︎ and Think v0.23.0 ↗︎ or later. Refer to the computer-skills ↗︎ and r2-skills ↗︎ examples.

Oct 28, 2026

Agents SDK: Preview dev servers in the browser without public URLs

AgentsBrowser Run

Agents that build websites need to check their work in a real browser. Internal hostnames let your agent's browser preview a dev server running in a container without exposing that server to the public Internet.

With internal hostnames, the persistent browser in the Cloudflare Agents SDK can open sites that only your agent serves. Give the browser hostnames such as preview.internal, and its requests to them go to your agent instead of the Internet. The model can check a dev server in its sandbox, a folder in its workspace, or another Worker in the same browser it uses for the web, and nothing is exposed publicly.

Each internal host has a fetch function that runs in your Durable Object, so it can use the object's bindings and state. A host can also send its requests straight to another Worker through a service binding. Add a target schema to a host, and the model chooses what it serves, such as which port or which folder.

Internal hostnames are a capability of the browser, independent of your agent harness. Use the built-in adapters for Pi Durable, AI SDK, and TanStack AI, or connect another harness by implementing a tool with browser.session(). No prebuilt adapter is required.

This example adds a private dev-server preview to a Pi Durable agent. Start with that guide's packages, bindings, and request handler, and install Agents SDK v0.31.0 ↗︎ or later. The example has three parts:

  • Browser configuration: internalHosts defines how the browser reaches the dev server.
  • Durable Object wiring: Lifecycle and fetchInternalHost() connect the browser to your application.
  • Harness integration: browserTool from agents/browser/pi registers the tool with Pi.

To use another harness, keep the browser configuration. Choose a browser-tool adapter if one is available, or implement a tool using browser.session().

browserTool tells the model about each host, including the schema of its target. Because preview.internal has a target schema, the model can choose which port it serves. To check its dev server, the model calls browser.assignHost() with a target that matches the schema, such as { port: 5173 }, and opens the URL it gets back:

The target is checked against the schema and stored, so it lasts across turns, browser restarts, and redeploys. Each request to http://preview.internal/ then calls the host's fetch function with { port: 5173 }.

This release also simplifies browserTool. It runs the model's code in its own Dynamic Worker and no longer needs a CodemodeRuntime export. Refer to the v0.31.0 upgrade notes ↗︎ if you already use browserTool.

For the complete example, limits, and security guidance, refer to Internal hostnames.

Oct 26, 2026

Cloudflare Computer now helps agents recover from interruptions and wait for approval

AgentsWorkers

@cloudflare/computer ↗︎ gives your agent a workspace to run code in. From v0.7.0, that code can resume after a deploy or crash, and pause on an external action, for example to approve a tool call.

Resume interrupted runs

Set onInterrupt: "replay" on WorkerJavaScriptBackend, or on a single run.

When recovery is triggered, the JavaScript runs again from the beginning, reusing recorded results for completed calls without printing previously recorded output again. If a call's result was not recorded before the interruption, recovery may repeat the call — even if its action already succeeded. For retry handling, including unsafeToRepeat() for operations that cannot safely repeat, refer to Calls that must not run twice.

Recovery starts on the next call to workspace.runtime. To recover without waiting for traffic, call workspace.runtime.recover() from a Durable Object alarm.

Wait for approvals

Expose your application functions through custom modules. A function can call ctx.interrupt() to pause the run until your application supplies an approval decision.

Require approval before posting a comment

For example, to provide a GitHub module that allows an agent to post a comment on an issue with approval, an implementation of postComment could look like this:

Call it from agent code

When the agent's code calls postComment(), the run pauses at ctx.interrupt() until your app responds. The agent's code calls it like any other function:

Respond to the approval request

The time spent waiting does not count toward its timeout. The wait also survives deploys. Fetch the pending calls with workspace.runtime.pending() and resolve them with respond():

The run continues once all pending calls are resolved.

For setup, current limitations, and how replay works, refer to Resume runs after a restart.
